Q1: Nickel exhibits significant recognized hazards, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive effects (CMR), environmental concerns (ENV), inhalation toxicity (IHL), and organ/systemic effects (OGN), all classified at Tier 1 based on the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Additional data indicates expanded concerns for oral (ORL) and dermal/eye (SKN) hazards at Tier 2. The only remaining data gap is for endocrine disruption (EDC), which is currently data deficient at Tier 4.
Q2: Nickel is recognized on several prominent lists of concern due to its established hazards. It is listed under California's Proposition 65 for causing cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm, and is subject to EPA Drinking Water Standards. Furthermore, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classifies nickel as a Group 2B carcinogen, meaning it is possibly carcinogenic to humans.
Q3: Nickel is an exceptionally well-characterized chemical, supported by over 830,000 literature references, far exceeding the typical number for most substances. Its precise molecular formula "Ni" and classification as an "Element" indicate a clearly defined substance, and it is not considered an ill-defined UVCB. While there is one specific data gap for endocrine disruption, the extensive body of research strongly suggests a comprehensive understanding of its other hazard profiles.
